t: This is St Benet Paul's Wharf, a Welsh Anglican church in the City of London. It was destroyed in the Great Fire of 1666, then rebuilt to a design by Sir Christopher Wren, who was given the job of rebuilding fifty-two City churches. It is one of only four City churches to escape damage in the Second World War. Since 1556 it has been the official church of the College of Arms, and several officers of arms are buried here, including the herald and antiquarian William Wyrley and the genealogist Samson Lennard. The name honours Saint Benedict, founder of the Benedictine order.
